title: Crash before commit: the new owner re-reads, so records are processed twice
caption: c2 processes b0 and b1 from p1, dies before committing, and c1 takes over p1 from the last committed offset, 0.

messages.label: poll from offset 0
messages.note: c2 owns p1. Its committed offset is 0.

messages.label: process b0, b1
messages.note: The side effects (emails, DB writes) happen here.

messages.label: crash before commit
messages.note: The commit of offset 2 never happens, and c2's heartbeats stop.

messages.label: rebalance: you now own p1
messages.note: No heartbeat within the session timeout (about 10–45 s), so the coordinator reassigns c2's partitions. Consumption of p1 pauses meanwhile.

messages.label: poll from committed offset 0
messages.note: The only progress the group knows about is the committed offset.

messages.label: b0, b1 (again)
messages.note: b0 and b1 are processed a second time. That's at-least-once: the handler must be idempotent.

scenarios.name: Graceful shutdown
scenarios.summary: A planned stop (a deploy) commits first and leaves the group on purpose: the new owner starts at the right offset, with no duplicates and no long pause.

messages.label: commit offset 2
messages.note: On SIGTERM the consumer finishes its batch and commits before exiting.

messages.label: leave group
messages.note: An explicit leave: no waiting for the session timeout.

messages.label: poll from committed offset 2
messages.note: b0 and b1 are not re-read. Each record was processed once.

scenarios.name: Alternative: commit first
scenarios.summary: At-most-once: commit before processing. A crash then skips the batch instead of repeating it. No duplicates, but lost records.

messages.label: commit offset 2
messages.note: Committed before any work is done.

messages.label: crash before processing
messages.note: b0 and b1 were never handled.

messages.label: poll from committed offset 2
messages.note: The group believes b0 and b1 are done. They are skipped for good.

scenarios.name: Slow handler: storm
scenarios.summary: No crash: a handler that exceeds max.poll.interval gets its consumer kicked out, its commit is rejected and the batch is redone, again and again. Use smaller batches or a longer interval.

messages.label: 500 records
messages.note: A big batch, and each record calls a slow API.

messages.label: still processing at 5 min
messages.note: It hasn't polled within max.poll.interval (5 min by default), so it's considered stuck.

messages.label: rebalance: you now own p1
messages.note: c2 is removed from the group although it's alive.

messages.label: commit offset 500
messages.note: Rejected: c2 no longer owns p1. c1 re-reads the same 500 records, and can hit the same limit.

messages.label: cap max.poll.records
messages.note: Fix: fewer records per poll, a longer max.poll.interval, or hand slow work to a pool and pause the partition.
